memory_candidates.content: In this agent system, a brand-new script placed under agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/ (or scripts/tests/) does NOT reach the deployed .claude/scripts/ tree automatically -- deploy-headless.sh only installs files explicitly whitelisted in that extension's manifest.json 'scripts' array. A new script silently fails to deploy (no error, just absent from .claude/scripts/) until it is added to that whitelist. Always grep manifest.json for the new script's name after creating it and before relying on a deployed-tree test; add it alphabetically-near its closest sibling if the list isn't strictly sorted.

scripts/update-phase-status.sh's heading-status replacement (sed -i "${line_number}s/\[.*\]/[...]/") is GREEDY: if a plan phase's own title contains a literal square-bracket pair (e.g. inline-code like `errors[]`), the match spans from that bracket through the trailing status bracket, silently destroying everything in between including the rest of the title. Phase titles containing literal '[' or ']' characters (even inside backticks) are a hazard with this tool until it is fixed to anchor on the trailing bracket group specifically. Check the heading by eye after any update-phase-status.sh call on a phase whose title has this shape.

Never launch deploy-headless.sh (or verify-deploy.sh) in the background and then continue editing the same source-store files it is reading -- the deploy can capture a partial edit state, producing a deployed tree that is internally inconsistent (e.g. a lib file with N members paired with a standards doc still describing N-1). Finish all source-store edits for the phase first, THEN deploy, and treat the deploy as a synchronization point, not something to race against.
